 Game Analysis , Pre-Game Gameday: Raptors @ Timberwolves, October 25
 Two undefeated teams going at it.
 October 25, 2026 Mete Makarnaci Game 3 of 82 is here as the Toronto Raptors will once again be on the road and have yet another matchup of undefeated streaks on the line as this time they draw their toughest assignment yet, the Minnesota Timberwolves.
 Raptors outlook 
 Record: 2-0 (Tied 2nd in Eastern Conference) 
 Offensive Rating: 113.8 (11th) 
 Defensive Rating :88.6 (1st)
 Net Rating: 25.2 (1st) 
 Raptors previous results 
 @ Wizards 112-102 W
 vs. Bulls 135-92 W
 Toronto’s offensive rating tanked from 2nd to 11th after just one game as they only put up 112 points against the Washington Wizards, but their immaculate defensive rating has stayed put at a league-high 88.6, which is a whole seven points clear of second-place Oklahoma City Thunder. Their net rating is only two points clear of tonight’s opponent, the Minnesota Timberwolves, who, like the Washington Wizards, have a brand new roster that has changed a ton from last season. Three big storylines for the Raptors: can Scottie and RJ keep their streak of 20+ points alive, and how will Toronto’s defence hold up against one of the top offensive units in the NBA? Finally, can Toronto find their shooting stroke and have a successful night beyond the three-point line?
 Timberwolves outlook 
 Record: 2-0 (Tied 2nd in Western Conference) 
 Offensive Rating: 119.4 (6th) 
 Defensive Rating: 96.1 (3rd) 
 Net Rating: 23.3 (2nd)
Timberwolves previous results: 
 @ Magic 115-93 W
 @ Heat 131-106 W
 Minnesota has started their season with back-to-back blowout wins over two teams in Florida. This will be their home opener, and with the results and offseason moves that saw the team bring in LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga, it should be a loud one in the Target Center tonight. Their advanced stats are a bit similar to Toronto’s, as their offensive rating is lower than their defensive and net rating, so even though it’s really early on in the season, this should be a big test for both sides to see if they match up against contenders. Kuminga’s only gone for a combined 23 points in two games but we know he has a chance to have an explosive game and LaMelo Ball has combined for 33 points. The offence is still Anthony Edwards, though, as he had a monster 45-point game to open up their season against Miami. Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert round out their starting five as the two members of the lineup who are known for their defensive abilities.
